samples.summary: New CLI refuses any callback without the echoed nonce, so `wafflebase login` breaks against every backend that has not yet deployed the matching echo
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:307 rejects (403, without settling) a callback lacking the nonce. The other side of that contract is packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-134, which only echoes `&nonce=` when the state carries one — i.e. only from a backend built with this change. `@wafflebase/cli` is published to npm and `DEFAULT_SERVER` (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts) points at the hosted API, but any self-hosted or not-yet-deployed backend returns the old nonce-less redirect; the CLI then hangs for the full timeout and exits 2 (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:365-380). The backend side deliberately stayed permissive for old CLIs (github-auth.guard.ts:54-57), but the reverse skew (new CLI → old server) is a hard login failure. Acknowledged in docs/design/cli.md:902-905, so this may be an accepted tradeoff — flagged because the affected consumer (a deployed backend) is not in the diff.

samples.summary: SSRF gate silently changes behaviour for the un-diffed `slides export` (and `docs export`) callers: image `src` values on any internal host/port other than the configured API server now fail the export
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:214 builds `createImageFetcher({ serverBase: getConfig(opts).server })` with no `lookup`; `assertFetchableImageUrl` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:~290) now exempts only the configured server's resolved address *and* port. A self-hosted deployment whose documents embed images served from a sibling internal listener (object store, image CDN, another port on the same box, a `*.internal`/`*.local` name) previously exported fine and now fails with IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED. The in-repo backend streams images through the API origin (packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:78), so the common path is exempt — hence low confidence — but no other consumer of `createImageFetcher` was re-examined for the new precondition.

samples.summary: Guard now hard-400s any `/auth/github?mode=cli` request with a missing/invalid port, where it previously fell through to the normal web OAuth login
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:47-51 throws BadRequestException; the pre-change code only skipped state creation and let `super.canActivate` run the ordinary web flow. Callers outside the diff: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:82-95 still accepts and `void`s `mode`/`port` with a comment describing the guard as merely injecting a state token, and packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27 links to `/auth/github` (no `mode`, so unaffected). Any bookmark, old client or probe sending `?mode=cli` without a valid port now gets a 400 instead of a browser login; the controller comment at auth.controller.ts:89-91 is left describing the old contract.

samples.summary: Image fetches to the CLI's own (auth-protected) images endpoint send no Authorization header, and a resulting 401/403 is now reported as a system error telling the user to run `wafflebase login`
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:363 issues `fetchOrThrow(target, { redirect: 'manual' }, fetchImpl)` with no auth headers, while `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/images/:imageId` is behind `CombinedAuthGuard` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:24). The missing header pre-dates this change, but the classification does not: `httpError(401, ...)` (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:76) now turns that response into a SystemError/AUTH_ERROR with the login hint and exit 2, so `docs export`/`slides export` of a doc with server-hosted images reports a credential problem the user cannot fix by logging in.

finding.summary: New CLI refuses any callback without the echoed nonce, so `wafflebase login` breaks against every backend that has not yet deployed the matching echo
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:307 rejects (403, without settling) a callback lacking the nonce. The other side of that contract is packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-134, which only echoes `&nonce=` when the state carries one — i.e. only from a backend built with this change. `@wafflebase/cli` is published to npm and `DEFAULT_SERVER` (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts) points at the hosted API, but any self-hosted or not-yet-deployed backend returns the old nonce-less redirect; the CLI then hangs for the full timeout and exits 2 (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:365-380). The backend side deliberately stayed permissive for old CLIs (github-auth.guard.ts:54-57), but the reverse skew (new CLI → old server) is a hard login failure. Acknowledged in docs/design/cli.md:902-905, so this may be an accepted tradeoff — flagged because the affected consumer (a deployed backend) is not in the diff.

verdict.reason: All claimed code verified present. login.ts:306-315 rejects (403, without settling) any /callback lacking a matching nonce, and the CLI always sends one (login.ts:179-183). auth.controller.ts:130-135 appends `&nonce=` only when `state.nonce` is set, so a backend predating this change returns the old nonce-less loopback redirect. The CLI then waits the full 30s timeout and rejects with LoginError(EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR) (login.ts:362-381), surfaced as a process.exit by registerLoginCommand (login.ts:70-77) — a hard login failure for a new CLI against an un-upgraded or self-hosted backend. github-auth.guard.ts:54-57 confirms the deliberate tolerance runs only in the old-CLI/new-server direction, with no reciprocal tolerance. docs/design/cli.md:902-919 acknowledges the CLI-side enforcement and this exact failure mode, which documents the tradeoff but does not guard against it. One minor overstatement in the finding (the timeout yields a named cause, not a bare hang) does not change the outcome. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and a cross-deployment contract change whose affected consumer is invisible in the diff is squarely in the blast-radius lane.

finding.summary: SSRF gate silently changes behaviour for the un-diffed `slides export` (and `docs export`) callers: image `src` values on any internal host/port other than the configured API server now fail the export
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:214 builds `createImageFetcher({ serverBase: getConfig(opts).server })` with no `lookup`; `assertFetchableImageUrl` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:~290) now exempts only the configured server's resolved address *and* port. A self-hosted deployment whose documents embed images served from a sibling internal listener (object store, image CDN, another port on the same box, a `*.internal`/`*.local` name) previously exported fine and now fails with IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED. The in-repo backend streams images through the API origin (packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:78), so the common path is exempt — hence low confidence — but no other consumer of `createImageFetcher` was re-examined for the new precondition.

verdict.reason: The gate exists as described (image-fetcher.ts:291-322 exempts only the configured server by resolved address AND effectivePort, line 300), and both consumers do call createImageFetcher without `lookup` (slides.ts:214, docs.ts:273-275). But this is not a blast-radius defect: (a) no caller contract is broken — `lookup` is optional with a DNS default (image-fetcher.ts:29, 325-326, 349) and `ImageFetcherOptions` still requires only `serverBase`, return shape unchanged; (b) the un-diffed docs-export consumer was not "unconsidered" — the call site itself documents the gate (docs.ts:266-272) and the CLI design doc specifies the behaviour for the export pipelines, including the exact trade-off named in the finding: "the configured server is the one internal destination still allowed … Another port on the same host is not covered — the exemption is the API server, not the machine" (docs/design/cli.md:870-879) with IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED as the documented exit-1 class (docs/design/cli.md:881, 1179); (c) the substance of the complaint is that the guard is too strict, i.e. a security/design trade-off, which this lens explicitly defers ("whether the new guard is the right security design … you only care that something bypasses it"). Nothing bypasses the guard and no consumer is left broken or inconsistent, so it is out of scope for the blast-radius rubric.

finding.summary: Font downloads in the PDF export path still use raw `fetch`, so they bypass the new `fetchOrThrow` classification and report a network failure as exit 1
finding.evidence: `PdfFonts.defaultSource()` at packages/docs/src/export/pdf-fonts.ts:236 does `const res = await fetch(url)` and throws a plain `Error` on failure. This code runs inside the CLI: packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:68 calls `preloadKoreanFonts` → `fonts.load(key)` → this fetch (jsdelivr URLs from `DEFAULT_URLS`) for any document containing Korean text, and `docs export --format pdf` reaches it via packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts. The diff converted every CLI-owned call site to `fetchOrThrow` so that a transport failure becomes `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR')` → exit 2 (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:150), but this out-of-package call site was not considered: on an offline/proxied machine the throw is a plain `TypeError`/`Error`, `exitCodeFor` falls through to `EXIT_USER_ERROR`, and the CLI exits 1 for exactly the 'unreachable server' case the new contract (packages/cli/README.md:114) says must be 2. Fix belongs either here (inject a fetch impl) or by wrapping `fonts.load` in the CLI.

verdict.reason: The presence claim is false. `PdfFonts.defaultSource()` does not use raw `fetch`: pdf-fonts.ts:244 reads `const res = await this.fetchImpl(url);`, an injected transport declared at pdf-fonts.ts:170 (`fetchImpl?: typeof globalThis.fetch`), stored at :208 and defaulted at :212. Line 236, the line the finding cites, is `return buf;`. The remedy the finding proposes ("inject a fetch impl") is already implemented: the CLI constructs `new PdfFonts({ sources, fetchImpl: classifiedFontFetch(opts.fontFetch) })` at packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:103-106, and `classifiedFontFetch` (pdf-export.ts:27-46) routes every font download through `fetchOrThrow` (pdf-export.ts:37) plus `httpError` for non-OK. `fetchOrThrow` (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:161-170) converts a transport rejection — the offline/proxied DNS/refused/TLS case the finding describes — into `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR')`, whose `exitCode` is honoured by `exitCodeFor` (errors.ts:180-188), so the CLI exits 2, not 1. There is no unwrapped CLI path: `new PdfFonts` occurs exactly once in packages/cli/src (pdf-export.ts:103), and all `docs export --format pdf` call sites (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:289, 298, 304) go through `exportPdf`, which always wraps. The only other construction, packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:70 (`opts.fonts ?? new PdfFonts()`), is the browser default and is bypassed because the CLI passes `fonts` explicitly (pdf-export.ts:110-114). The preloadKoreanFonts -> fonts.load path (pdf-export.ts:170) therefore uses the classified transport.

finding.summary: The SSRF gate's single-origin allowance breaks CLI export for self-hosted/dev documents whose persisted absolute image URLs use a different spelling of the internal server than `--server`
finding.evidence: Image `src` values are persisted ABSOLUTE by the frontend: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:86-90 rewrites every backend image URL to `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}${path}` precisely so it survives persistence (`http://localhost:3000/...` in dev, an internal host in a self-hosted deployment). The new gate allows exactly one internal origin — `url.origin === serverOrigin` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:186) — and otherwise refuses any internal hostname (`.internal`/`.local`/`localhost`) or private/loopback address. So a document whose stored srcs say `http://localhost:3000/...` while the CLI is configured with `--server http://127.0.0.1:3000` (or a LAN IP vs hostname, or http vs https, or a differing port) now fails with `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` where `docs export`/`slides export` previously fetched the image fine. No fallback (e.g. allowing the same host under a different spelling, or an opt-in flag) exists.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the gate allows only an exact `url.origin === serverOrigin` match (cited at image-fetcher.ts:186) and that "no fallback (e.g. allowing the same host under a different spelling) exists". Both claims are false against the file. Line 186 is inside `isPrivateAddress`'s Teredo branch, not an origin check. The origin comparison lives at line 291 and is documented as a cheap fast path only. Lines 299-312 implement the exact fallback the finding says is missing: URLs whose effective port matches `--server` skip the internal-hostname refusal (line 306), are DNS-resolved (line 308), and are allowed when `sharesAddressWithServer` (lines 243-257) finds an address shared with the configured server. The comment at lines 231-242 names the reviewer's own scenario (doc stores `http://localhost:3000/...`, CLI run with `--server http://127.0.0.1:3000`) as the motivating case, and test/image-fetcher.test.ts:311-318 asserts that case fetches successfully. The frontend premise (image-upload.ts:86-90 persisting absolute URLs) is accurate but is precisely what the gate accommodates. The only residual refusal is a differing port/scheme-default port, which the code deliberately treats as a different listener (comment lines 293-298), and the reviewer cited no broken consumer for it.
